cases.literal_request: Add American Water Works FY2021 unadjusted operating income from the income statement to FY2021 depreciation and amortization from the cash flow statement, using the question's definition of unadjusted EBITDA.

interpretations.description: Use the reported, unadjusted operating income and the depreciation-and-amortization amount reported in the cash flow statement for the same FY2021 reporting entity and period.
required_facts: American Water Works FY2021 operating income as reported in the income statement.
Depreciation and amortization reported for FY2021 in the cash flow statement, including whether this is one combined line or multiple explicitly corresponding components.
The statements' reporting period, entity scope, currency and scale, sufficient to align the two figures and express the sum in USD millions.
assumptions: The company-wide question refers to the company's consolidated statements.
The explicit addition in the question controls the calculation; no further adjustments or substitute EBITDA definition are introduced.
ambiguities: No rounding precision is specified.

If multiple cash-flow amortization categories are separately reported, the question does not expressly resolve whether every such category belongs in its depreciation-and-amortization term; the statement labels would need to support the component selection.

cases.reason: The arithmetic definition, fiscal year and output currency are explicit. A unique result depends on identifying the corresponding reported depreciation-and-amortization amount without silently expanding it to unrelated cash-flow amortization categories.
cases.recognition_or_prior_knowledge: I recognize the company name and have general knowledge of financial statement terminology. No specific benchmark item, reference answer or FY2021 value recalled; no remembered answer used.

cases.literal_request: Calculate Coca Cola FY2017 ROA as FY2017 net income divided by average total assets between FY2016 and FY2017, relying on the balance sheet and P&L, and round to two decimal places.

output_contract.units: Dimensionless; decimal-ratio versus percentage presentation is not specified.
output_contract.precision: Two decimal places; the presentation scale must be identified because rounding a decimal ratio and rounding a percentage differ.

interpretations.description: Use consolidated net income and the arithmetic mean of consolidated fiscal-year-end total assets for FY2016 and FY2017.
required_facts: Consolidated FY2017 net income from the P&L statement.
Consolidated total assets at the end of FY2016 from the balance sheet.
Consolidated total assets at the end of FY2017 from the balance sheet.
Statement labels, fiscal dates, entity scope and measurement units sufficient to establish comparable numerator and denominator inputs.
assumptions: Coca Cola refers to The Coca-Cola Company.
Average total assets means the arithmetic mean of the two fiscal-year-end balances, rather than an average of interim balances.
Net income means consolidated net income, including any noncontrolling-interest share, if separately distinguished.
ambiguities: The question does not qualify net income as consolidated or attributable to the parent company.
The decimal-ratio versus percentage display convention is unspecified.

interpretations.description: Use FY2017 net income attributable to the parent company with the same average consolidated total-assets denominator, if the question uses net income in that attributable-income sense.
required_facts: FY2017 net income attributable to the parent company, as distinguished in the P&L statement.
Consolidated total assets at the end of FY2016 from the balance sheet.
Consolidated total assets at the end of FY2017 from the balance sheet.
The P&L attribution labels and comparable fiscal periods, entity scope and measurement units for the selected figures.
assumptions: Coca Cola refers to The Coca-Cola Company.
Average total assets means the arithmetic mean of the two fiscal-year-end balances.
The otherwise unqualified net-income term is intended to mean income attributable to the parent.
ambiguities: The question does not establish the parent-attributable numerator in preference to consolidated net income.
The decimal-ratio versus percentage display convention is unspecified.

cases.reason: The denominator formula and requested precision substantially constrain the task, but the net-income attribution and ratio display scale must be made explicit. The two numerator interpretations may coincide if the statements contain no relevant attribution distinction.
cases.recognition_or_prior_knowledge: I recognize the company name and recall general ROA and financial statement conventions. No specific benchmark item, reference answer or FY2017 value recalled; no remembered answer used.

cases.literal_request: Read Costco total assets at the end of FY2021 from the balance sheet and report the amount in USD millions.

output_contract.type: monetary balance at a fiscal-year-end date

interpretations.description: Use the total-assets balance in Costco's consolidated balance sheet for its FY2021 closing date.
required_facts: The balance-sheet column corresponding to Costco's FY2021 year end.
The total-assets amount in that column.
The balance sheet's reporting entity, currency and unit scale, sufficient to express the balance in USD millions.
assumptions: Costco refers to Costco Wholesale Corporation and the company-wide request refers to its consolidated balance sheet.
End of FY2021 means the company's fiscal-year closing date, not an assumed calendar-year closing date.
ambiguities: No rounding precision is specified; retaining the balance sheet's reported precision after unit conversion is a reporting choice.

cases.reason: The requested line item, fiscal-year-end basis, allowed statement and output units are explicit. Under the ordinary company-level reading, no additional financial metric convention is needed.
cases.recognition_or_prior_knowledge: I recognize Costco as a company name and know general balance-sheet terminology. No specific benchmark item, reference answer or FY2021 balance recalled; no remembered answer used.

cases.literal_request: Identify the 3M segment that dragged down overall growth in 2022 after excluding M&A effects.

output_contract.type: segment identification, with the basis for judging a growth drag
output_contract.precision: Not specified; the question uses singular which segment but does not establish that exactly one qualifies.

interpretations.description: Identify a segment with negative year-over-year sales growth after removing acquisitions and divestitures from reported growth, while retaining other effects such as currency.
required_facts: The segments in the relevant 2022 reporting structure and comparable prior-year structure.
Each segment's 2022 sales growth relative to the comparison period.
Each segment's acquisition and divestiture effects on that growth, or an explicitly reported sales-growth measure excluding them.
The sign and comparable definition of the resulting segment growth measures.
assumptions: Growth means sales growth and 2022 means the full reporting year compared with 2021.
M&A exclusion includes acquisitions and divestitures.
Dragged down means an absolute decline in a segment, rather than merely slower growth than the company.
Currency and other non-M&A effects remain included.
ambiguities: The question does not specify sales rather than earnings, profit or another measure of growth.
It does not explicitly specify the comparison period.
More than one segment might decline; the singular wording gives no tie-breaking rule.
Excluding M&A does not itself establish whether currency effects should also be excluded.

interpretations.description: Identify a segment with negative organic sales growth, where an organic-growth definition may exclude currency as well as acquisitions and divestitures.
required_facts: The relevant 2022 segments and their comparable 2022 organic sales growth rates.
The actual definition of organic sales growth, including acquisition, divestiture and currency treatment.
The period and comparison basis for those growth rates.
Which segments have negative growth on that consistently defined basis.
assumptions: Growth means sales growth for full-year 2022 versus 2021.
Excluding M&A is intended as shorthand for an organic-growth measure, although the wording alone does not establish any additional exclusions.
Dragged down means a segment's own growth was negative.
ambiguities: An organic measure that also removes currency can yield a different conclusion from removing only M&A.
The question supplies no organic-growth definition or rule for choosing among multiple declining segments.

interpretations.description: Identify a segment whose M&A-adjusted growth lagged the company's overall growth and therefore lowered the company's aggregate growth rate relative to the other segments, even if the segment itself grew.
required_facts: A defined growth metric and consistently M&A-adjusted segment growth rates for the same 2022 comparison period.
Company-wide growth measured on the same basis.
Comparable prior-period segment sizes or explicit contribution data needed to relate segment growth to overall growth.
Any reconciliation items or scope differences material to aggregating segment growth into company growth.
assumptions: Growth means full-year sales growth versus the prior year.
Dragged down means underperformed the aggregate, rather than contracted in absolute terms.
The company and segment measures use the same M&A and currency treatment.
ambiguities: The question does not choose between any below-average segment, the lowest growth rate, or the greatest weighted drag.
A segment can be a relative drag without negative growth.
A unique segment cannot be presumed from the singular wording.

cases.reason: The question leaves the growth metric, comparison basis, non-M&A treatment and meaning of dragged down unresolved. Plausible absolute-decline, organic-decline and relative-contribution readings require different facts and can identify different segments.
cases.recognition_or_prior_knowledge: I recognize 3M and recall general segment-growth and acquisition-adjustment concepts. No specific benchmark item, reference answer, 2022 segment outcome or numeric value recalled; no remembered answer used.

cases.literal_request: Estimate JnJ FY2022 inventory turnover as a number of times inventory was sold, or state and explain why conventional inventory management is not meaningful for the company if that condition applies.

output_contract.type: inventory-turnover ratio, or an explanation of inapplicability if supported
output_contract.units: Times per FY2022 for the ratio; currency is not an output unit.
output_contract.precision: Roughly; no required number of decimal places.

interpretations.description: Use the conventional cost-based inventory-turnover measure: FY2022 cost of goods sold or the corresponding cost-of-sales measure divided by average inventory, subject to assessing whether the measure is meaningful.
required_facts: FY2022 cost of goods sold or a corresponding inventory-related cost-of-sales amount, with its financial statement definition.
Inventory balances at the beginning and end of FY2022 for the same reporting scope, if a two-point average is used.
Compatible measurement units and entity scope for costs and inventory, including any material reporting-scope change.
The nature and role of inventory and sales in the company's business, sufficient to determine whether conventional inventory turnover is meaningful and to explain any conclusion of inapplicability.
assumptions: JnJ refers to Johnson & Johnson.
Inventory turnover uses costs rather than sales revenue in its numerator.
Average inventory is approximated by the arithmetic mean of the opening and closing FY2022 balances.
The question refers to the consolidated company rather than a particular segment.
ambiguities: The question supplies neither a turnover formula nor an averaging convention; a more frequent within-year average may differ from the two-point approximation.
It provides no criterion for declaring conventional inventory management not meaningful.
Roughly does not establish a fixed rounding precision.

interpretations.description: Estimate turnover using FY2022 cost of goods sold divided by FY2022 closing inventory as a simplified period-end inventory proxy.
required_facts: FY2022 cost of goods sold or corresponding inventory-related cost-of-sales amount.
Inventory at the FY2022 closing date.
Compatible reporting scope and measurement units for the cost and inventory figures.
The nature and role of inventory in the business, sufficient to assess meaningfulness and to explain any conclusion of inapplicability.
assumptions: JnJ refers to Johnson & Johnson and the request is company-wide.
Closing inventory is an acceptable proxy for average inventory; this approximation must be disclosed.
Inventory turnover uses costs rather than sales revenue.
ambiguities: The question does not authorize a closing-balance proxy in preference to average inventory.
Roughly concerns precision but does not by itself settle the denominator convention.
The criterion for meaningful conventional inventory management remains unspecified.

interpretations.description: Read sold its inventory as a sales-based turnover measure, using FY2022 sales divided by average inventory, while explicitly distinguishing this from conventional cost-based inventory turnover.
required_facts: FY2022 sales revenue for the relevant reporting entity.
Opening and closing FY2022 inventory balances for the same scope if a two-point average is used.
Compatible measurement units and the valuation basis of inventory, to explain that revenue and inventory are measured on different bases.
The role of inventory in the business, sufficient to assess whether this turnover interpretation is meaningful.
assumptions: JnJ refers to Johnson & Johnson and the request is company-wide.
The ordinary-language sales wording is intended to select a sales numerator despite the explicit request for an inventory-turnover ratio.
Average inventory means the arithmetic mean of opening and closing balances.
ambiguities: This is a less compelling interpretation than conventional cost-based inventory turnover, but the question supplies no formula.
A sales-based ratio cannot be silently treated as equivalent to a cost-based ratio.
No explicit meaningfulness criterion or numeric precision is provided.

cases.reason: A conventional cost-based interpretation is available, but the formula, inventory averaging method and meaningfulness criterion are not explicitly established. The result requires stating the adopted convention; inapplicability requires business evidence, not merely missing figures.
cases.recognition_or_prior_knowledge: I recognize JnJ as a common abbreviation for Johnson & Johnson and recall general inventory-turnover conventions. No specific benchmark item, reference answer or FY2022 financial amount recalled; no remembered answer used. I have not used remembered business details to decide whether the conditional exception applies.

cases.literal_request: Judge whether Verizon is a capital-intensive business using FY2022 evidence.

output_contract.type: qualitative yes/no assessment supported by FY2022 data; a qualified conclusion may be necessary
output_contract.units: No numeric unit or ratio requested.

interpretations.description: Assess capital intensity as the scale of FY2022 capital expenditure relative to the company's operating scale, such as revenue.
required_facts: FY2022 capital expenditure with a definition of included investments.
FY2022 revenue or another explicitly selected, economically justified scale measure for the same entity.
Compatible reporting units, period and scope for the expenditure and scale measure.
A stated evaluative basis for calling the resulting investment requirement intensive, such as a justified comparison or qualitative standard.
assumptions: Verizon refers to Verizon Communications and the question is company-wide.
Capital intensity is being judged by current-period capital spending relative to business scale.
Any selected denominator, investment scope and comparison standard are analytical choices, not supplied by the question.
ambiguities: No spending definition, denominator or classification threshold is specified.
The treatment of intangible investment and acquisitions is not specified.
A single year's spending may not uniquely characterize the ongoing investment requirements of the business.

interpretations.description: Assess capital intensity as the amount and nature of long-lived operating assets required to generate the company's output, using FY2022 asset and operating data.
required_facts: FY2022 balances and classifications for relevant long-lived operating assets.
FY2022 total assets or revenue, if an asset-share or asset-to-output comparison is used.
Gross versus net carrying basis, period alignment and reporting scope for the selected measures.
Evidence relating the relevant assets to business operations.
An explicit qualitative or comparative basis for classifying the required asset base as capital intensive.
assumptions: Verizon refers to Verizon Communications and the question is company-wide.
Capital intensity is being judged by the required operating-asset base rather than current-year spending alone.
Which tangible or intangible assets count, and whether balances are closing or average balances, must be selected and disclosed if used.
ambiguities: The question specifies no asset definition, valuation basis, ratio or threshold.
A large absolute asset balance alone does not establish intensity relative to business scale.
Asset-base and current-spending interpretations can support different assessments and are not interchangeable.

cases.reason: The question supports an evidence-based qualitative assessment, but it does not determine a unique numerical test or classification threshold. A defensible answer must state its basis and support that basis with FY2022 facts without treating an invented cutoff as given.
cases.recognition_or_prior_knowledge: I recognize Verizon and recall general capital-intensity concepts. No specific benchmark item, reference answer or FY2022 financial value recalled; no remembered answer used. I have not used remembered industry characteristics to preselect a conclusion.
